inVia PickerWall

your fulfillment reality

inVia PickerWall is a dynamic pick/put wall our robots build with each day’s orders. The robots work
in rote fashion on one side of the wall, while people work in bursts on the other side, pulling
products and sorting them into order bins. Costly warehouse walking is eliminated and workers can
rotate freely across other warehouse tasks.

with simple instructions

directs warehouse workers to quickly and accurately pick and place goods that are moving through the
order process.

# Flexibility-First
# Automation

Flexible automation that adapts to demand fluctuations, workforce shifts, and evolving order

## Fully autonomous fulfillment starts with Locus Array

*A new class of Physical AI for high-performance warehouse automation.* 

Engineered to perceive, reason, and act in real time, [Locus Array
][120]executes [autonomous fulfillment][121] directly in the aisle through a Robots-to-Goods (R2G)
model. From picking and putaway to induction, drop-off, slotting, and replenishment, fulfillment
runs continuously across every shift. 

Orchestrated by LocusONE™, Locus Array executes the work that keeps fulfillment running around the
clock. Throughput stays high, storage density increases, and time to value accelerates, even when
demand shifts without warning. No rigidity. No long lead times. And none of the constraints that
come with traditional fixed automation. 

[ See How Locus Array Works ][122]
[Locus Array in aisles]

## Modern warehouse operations no longer operate in predictable cycles

Order volumes surge and soften without warning. SKU profiles evolve continuously. Labor availability
changes by shift, by role, and by location. What once could be planned months in advance now must be
managed in real time.

In this environment, the question is no longer how fast you can run. It’s whether you can keep
running when conditions shift. It requires the confidence and ability to maintain throughput,
service levels, and execution quality even as conditions change.

Locus Robotics enables scalable fulfillment automation by orchestrating people and warehouse robots
as one intelligent workforce. Our autonomous mobile robots reduce travel time, improve picking
efficiency, and help maintain throughput even during peak variability.

[ Improve Your Business ][123]

## Automation Built for Change

Traditional warehouse automation is built for predictability. Today’s operations are not.

Locus Robotics takes a different approach.

Our flexible automation model combines physical AI, real-time orchestration, and adaptive execution
to continuously rebalance work inside the warehouse. As priorities shift throughout the day,
[LocusONE][124]™ dynamically coordinates work across associates and robots to keep operations
moving.

The result is stable throughput — even when demand spikes or labor tightens.

#### Adapt Across Environments

Deploy warehouse robotics in existing facilities, multi-level operations, and evolving layouts
without costly redesigns.

#### Scale at Your Pace

Start where you need today and expand automation as volume, workflows, and business demands grow.

#### Maintain Operational Confidence

Sustain throughput and service levels despite variability in labor, demand, and order complexity.

## Flexible Fulfillment Across Core Workflows

Every warehouse faces variability — in volume, labor, inventory, and order mix. Locus Robotics
adapts across these realities by coordinating work dynamically across the most critical fulfillment
workflows.

physical AI to continuously coordinate work across people, autonomous robots, and workflows —
balancing priorities, reallocating labor, and protecting throughput as conditions change. Powered by
LocusONE’s physical AI, Locus Robotics delivers multiple automation paths designed to match
operational reality:

Guided by LocusONE, Locus Origin and Locus Vector work alongside associates to support picking,
transport, and fulfillment workflows across the warehouse.

[LEARN MORE][136]

With Locus Array, operations can reduce picking and putaway labor by 90%+ and introduce highly
autonomous execution where it makes sense - without rebuilding the facility or replacing existing
systems. Together, these solutions allow warehouses to automate in phases — without locking into a
single path.

From global 3PLs to enterprise retailers and healthcare distributors, organizations rely on Locus
Robotics to deliver consistent performance at scale.

* Faster onboarding when labor pools fluctuate
* Improved labor utilization across shifting workflows
* Measurable productivity gains without rigid automation

FAQ

## Answers to your most pressing questions

[
How can Delivery Robots navigate through obstacles and people?
][17]

Relay robots are equipped with an advanced sensor suite that includes cameras, lidars and various
other safety sensors. These sensors continuously scan the environment and form a high quality
dynamic map of the surrounding area. This gives the robot exceptional spatial awareness and allows
it to plan a safe path through all obstacles and people. Even sudden changes like a child abruptly
jumping onto its path appears on this map prompting Relay to respond within milliseconds.

[
Can Delivery Robots guarantee chain of custody for sensitive items?
][18]

Relay’s authentication options provide pharmacists with a verifiable trail for every medication
delivered throughout the hospital. Additionally, sophisticated software and “Uber-like” maps show
real-time delivery status while tracking and reporting delivery history.

[
How do Delivery Robot batteries get charged?
][19]

Every Relay comes with a charging dock that can be placed strategically at the site. As Relays go
about their tasks, they are continuously monitoring their battery levels and are always recharging
between deliveries such that the battery rarely runs low. however, if the battery is low, they
autonomously navigate to the dock and automatically dock themselves until charged.

[
How do Delivery Robots access an elevator?
][20]

During installation, elevators are configured to communicate with Relay robots. This allows them to
call elevators, select their destination, enter and exit the elevators, and complete deliveries

## Answers to your most pressing questions

[
How can Delivery Robots navigate through obstacles and people?
][17]

Relay robots are equipped with an advanced sensor suite that includes cameras, lidars and various
other safety sensors. These sensors continuously scan the environment and form a high quality
dynamic map of the surrounding area. This gives the robot exceptional spatial awareness and allows
it to plan a safe path through all obstacles and people. Even sudden changes like a child abruptly
jumping onto its path appears on this map prompting Relay to respond within milliseconds.

[
Can Delivery Robots guarantee chain of custody for sensitive items?
][18]

Relay’s authentication options provide pharmacists with a verifiable trail for every medication
delivered throughout the hospital. Additionally, sophisticated software and “Uber-like” maps show
real-time delivery status while tracking and reporting delivery history.

[
How do Delivery Robot batteries get charged?
][19]

Every Relay comes with a charging dock that can be placed strategically at the site. As Relays go
about their tasks, they are continuously monitoring their battery levels and are always recharging
between deliveries such that the battery rarely runs low. however, if the battery is low, they
autonomously navigate to the dock and automatically dock themselves until charged.

# Autonomy
# That Works

## AI-Powered Autonomous Mobile Robots

We are more than just a leading-edge technology company—we are the pioneers of Physical AI for
[industrial material handling][47]. By running advanced perception models directly onboard our
autonomous mobile robots, we deliver [reliable AMRs built for busy, changing industrial
environments.][48] Achieve new heights of efficiency, [safety][49], and proven automation ROI.

[ Let's Start Your Autonomous Journey ][50]

## Meet Our AMR Fleet

Optimize facility workflows and transform material handling with Seegrid AMRs, enhancing
productivity and reducing costs through seamless, connected autonomous solutions.

### [ Seegrid Lift EL1 AMR ][51]

**Best For:** Space-constrained warehousing, 3PL, and large retail fulfillment centers

**Max Lift Height:** 5' 2"

**Payload Capacity:** 2,500 lbs

**Key Applications:** Inbound to putaway or buffer, pick/drop to wrappers and/or conveyors, cross
docking, outbound staging

**Highlight:** Interoperability-ready with full VDA 5050 compliance

[ Bring Interoperability To My Facility ][52]

### [ Seegrid Lift RS1 AMR ][53]

**Best For:** Low-lift applications across industrial manufacturing and warehousing environments

**Max Lift Height:** 6'

**Payload Capacity:** 3,500 lbs

**Key Applications:** Buffer management, material transport, parts-to-line, outbound, cross docking

**Highlight:** Industry-leading payload detection

[ Experience Maximum Throughput ][54]

### [ Seegrid Lift CR1 AMR ][55]

**Best For:** Heavy manufacturing environments

**Max Lift Height:** 15'

**Payload Capacity:** 4,000 lbs

**Key Applications:** Buffer management, material transport, vertical handling, robotic cell
integration, and parts-to-line delivery

**Highlight:** Ride-on compartment for even greater flexibility

[ Go Higher & Heavier ][56]

### [ Seegrid Tow Tractor S7 AMR ][57]

**Best For:** All industrial environments, including warehousing, manufacturing, and logistics

**Payload Capacity:** 10,000 lbs

**Key Applications:** Long-haul cart train tugging, parts-to-line, replenishment, putaway,
cross-docking, dunnage/trash removal

# Autonomy
# That Works

## AI-Powered Autonomous Mobile Robots

We are more than just a leading-edge technology company—we are the pioneers of Physical AI for
[industrial material handling][47]. By running advanced perception models directly onboard our
autonomous mobile robots, we deliver [reliable AMRs built for busy, changing industrial
environments.][48] Achieve new heights of efficiency, [safety][49], and proven automation ROI.

[ Let's Start Your Autonomous Journey ][50]

## Meet Our AMR Fleet

Optimize facility workflows and transform material handling with Seegrid AMRs, enhancing
productivity and reducing costs through seamless, connected autonomous solutions.

### [ Seegrid Lift EL1 AMR ][51]

**Best For:** Space-constrained warehousing, 3PL, and large retail fulfillment centers

**Max Lift Height:** 5' 2"

**Payload Capacity:** 2,500 lbs

**Key Applications:** Inbound to putaway or buffer, pick/drop to wrappers and/or conveyors, cross
docking, outbound staging

**Highlight:** Interoperability-ready with full VDA 5050 compliance

[ Bring Interoperability To My Facility ][52]

### [ Seegrid Lift RS1 AMR ][53]

**Best For:** Low-lift applications across industrial manufacturing and warehousing environments

**Max Lift Height:** 6'

**Payload Capacity:** 3,500 lbs

**Key Applications:** Buffer management, material transport, parts-to-line, outbound, cross docking

**Highlight:** Industry-leading payload detection

[ Experience Maximum Throughput ][54]

### [ Seegrid Lift CR1 AMR ][55]

**Best For:** Heavy manufacturing environments

**Max Lift Height:** 15'

**Payload Capacity:** 4,000 lbs

**Key Applications:** Buffer management, material transport, vertical handling, robotic cell
integration, and parts-to-line delivery

**Highlight:** Ride-on compartment for even greater flexibility

[ Go Higher & Heavier ][56]

### [ Seegrid Tow Tractor S7 AMR ][57]

**Best For:** All industrial environments, including warehousing, manufacturing, and logistics

**Payload Capacity:** 10,000 lbs

**Key Applications:** Long-haul cart train tugging, parts-to-line, replenishment, putaway,
cross-docking, dunnage/trash removal

**Highlight:** Most proven and battle-tested form factor, Seegrid's Autonomous Tow Tractor holds #1
market share in the U.S.

* Seamless future planning powered by AI-driven BI softwares

### Automated Guided Vehicle Supplier Directory Overview

Find, compare, and connect with automated guided vehicle manufacturers through a supplier directory
built to help buyers source the right automation partner for material movement, pallet transport,
cart handling, towing, and line support. This page is designed for teams that need to browse AGV
manufacturers, review AGV suppliers, and compare automated guided vehicles for warehousing,
manufacturing, automotive production, healthcare logistics, food processing, and distribution
operations. Whether you are planning a first deployment or expanding an AGV system, this directory
helps buyers quickly identify suppliers by equipment type, application focus, and operational fit.

### Forklift-Style Automated Guided Vehicles

Forklift-style automated guided vehicles are built for pallet pickup, drop-off, stacking support,
and repetitive load transfer in warehouses, factories, and shipping areas. Buyers often compare
these systems when they need automated guided vehicle manufacturers that support higher payloads,
aisle navigation, and safer material movement around workers and fixed equipment.

### Tugger and Cart-Based AGV Systems

Tugger and cart-based automated guided vehicles are used to pull trailers, move work-in-process
materials, and feed production areas on scheduled routes. These AGV vehicles are common in
manufacturing plants, automotive operations, and large assembly environments where continuous parts
flow, route repeatability, and predictable delivery timing matter.

### Unit Load Vehicles and Automated Guided Carts

Unit load vehicles and automated guided carts support tote movement, pallet transfer, and
station-to-station transport across distribution, packaging, electronics, and pharmaceutical
operations. Buyers searching AGV manufacturers and AGV companies often look at load type, routing
method, and facility layout to determine whether a standard vehicle or more specialized automated
guided vehicle system makes the most sense.

### Autonomous Guided Vehicles and AGV Robots

More advanced autonomous guided vehicle and AGV robot platforms support flexible navigation,
obstacle detection, and software-driven fleet coordination. These systems are frequently used in
facilities that want greater route adaptability, better traffic control, and easier integration with
warehouse software, manufacturing controls, and changing workflows.

### Industry Applications of AGV Systems

Automotive plants rely on automated guided vehicles to move parts, kits, and assemblies between
storage areas and production cells with predictable timing. Warehousing and distribution operations
use AGV robots for pallet transport, replenishment, and order movement across high-volume
facilities. Food and beverage processors depend on automated guided vehicle systems for repeatable
material flow in fast-paced production environments. Healthcare facilities use autonomous guided
vehicles to move supplies, carts, and support materials through controlled internal routes.
Electronics and pharmaceutical manufacturers use AGV vehicle platforms where clean handling,
accuracy, and traceable movement are essential.

### Production Volume and System Design Fit

Production volume should shape the starting point of any supplier review. Buyers comparing AGV
suppliers should define throughput, shift patterns, load frequency, and route density before
narrowing options, because a low-volume transport task and a continuous high-volume workflow require
very different system designs.

### Fixed Route vs Flexible Navigation Systems

Process type matters just as much as speed. Some operations need fixed, repeatable routes for line
feeding or pallet transfer, while others benefit from more flexible autonomous guided vehicle or AMR
manufacturers that support dynamic rerouting, variable tasks, and mixed traffic conditions.

### Integration with Existing Facility Systems

Integration planning should happen early. Buyers should ask whether an AGV system can connect with
existing conveyors, racking layouts, software controls, scanners, safety systems, and production
scheduling tools without creating bottlenecks or forcing major floor changes.

### Compliance, Safety, and Documentation Requirements

Inspection, documentation, and compliance review should also be part of vendor evaluation.
Facilities in regulated or quality-sensitive industries often need suppliers that can support
validation requirements, safety documentation, testing standards, and clear maintenance practices
alongside the equipment itself.

### Choosing the Right AGV Manufacturer

Supplier specialization can separate a workable project from an expensive mismatch. When reviewing
AGV manufacturers, AGV companies, AMR companies, or AMR robot companies, buyers should compare
application experience, payload focus, navigation approach, support responsiveness, and ability to
scale from one vehicle to a larger fleet.

### Unit Load Vehicles and Automated Guided Carts

Unit load vehicles and automated guided carts support tote movement, pallet transfer, and
station-to-station transport across distribution, packaging, electronics, and pharmaceutical
operations. Buyers searching AGV manufacturers and AGV companies often look at load type, routing
method, and facility layout to determine whether a standard vehicle or more specialized automated
guided vehicle system makes the most sense.

### Autonomous Guided Vehicles and AGV Robots

More advanced autonomous guided vehicle and AGV robot platforms support flexible navigation,
obstacle detection, and software-driven fleet coordination. These systems are frequently used in
facilities that want greater route adaptability, better traffic control, and easier integration with
warehouse software, manufacturing controls, and changing workflows.

### Industry Applications of AGV Systems

Automotive plants rely on automated guided vehicles to move parts, kits, and assemblies between
storage areas and production cells with predictable timing. Warehousing and distribution operations
use AGV robots for pallet transport, replenishment, and order movement across high-volume
facilities. Food and beverage processors depend on automated guided vehicle systems for repeatable
material flow in fast-paced production environments. Healthcare facilities use autonomous guided
vehicles to move supplies, carts, and support materials through controlled internal routes.
Electronics and pharmaceutical manufacturers use AGV vehicle platforms where clean handling,
accuracy, and traceable movement are essential.

### Production Volume and System Design Fit

Production volume should shape the starting point of any supplier review. Buyers comparing AGV
suppliers should define throughput, shift patterns, load frequency, and route density before
narrowing options, because a low-volume transport task and a continuous high-volume workflow require
very different system designs.

### Fixed Route vs Flexible Navigation Systems

Process type matters just as much as speed. Some operations need fixed, repeatable routes for line
feeding or pallet transfer, while others benefit from more flexible autonomous guided vehicle or AMR
manufacturers that support dynamic rerouting, variable tasks, and mixed traffic conditions.

### Integration with Existing Facility Systems

Integration planning should happen early. Buyers should ask whether an AGV system can connect with
existing conveyors, racking layouts, software controls, scanners, safety systems, and production
scheduling tools without creating bottlenecks or forcing major floor changes.

### Compliance, Safety, and Documentation Requirements

Inspection, documentation, and compliance review should also be part of vendor evaluation.
Facilities in regulated or quality-sensitive industries often need suppliers that can support
validation requirements, safety documentation, testing standards, and clear maintenance practices
alongside the equipment itself.

### Choosing the Right AGV Manufacturer

Supplier specialization can separate a workable project from an expensive mismatch. When reviewing
AGV manufacturers, AGV companies, AMR companies, or AMR robot companies, buyers should compare
application experience, payload focus, navigation approach, support responsiveness, and ability to
scale from one vehicle to a larger fleet.

The AutoStore warehouse automation system is the pinnacle of speed, density, and accuracy for

efficiency][156] is redefined. Robots replace aisles with dense, scalable storage, multiplying
capacity without expanding your footprint. Adaptable to any space, AutoStore integrates seamlessly,
ensuring high-speed, accurate operations with minimal energy.

Expandable and reliable, it’s the smart warehousing solution that keeps everything within reach,
revolutionizing inventory management globally. Embrace the cube revolution — where every inch
counts, every item is within arm’s length, and every order moves fast.

## Robotic Solutions

Physical AI Training Platform

Enable robots to learn from physical interaction — not just vision or simulation.

High-fidelity force and torque data provides a critical modality for Physical AI, supporting
kinesthetic teaching, teleoperation, and the collection of high-quality datasets for learning-based

making manipulation more precise and intuitive.

 

By combining high-resolution sensing with low-latency response, it enhances safety, reduces

Best for Hazardous environments, multiple follower devices and remote access.

capturing synchronized motion, force, tactile, and visual data in real time

FORCE SENSING IN REAL-WORLD APPLICATIONS

## Robotic Solutions

From manufacturing to research, our force torque sensors enable precise, adaptive robot behavior
across industrial automation and Physical AI applications. Our ***turnkey solutions*** minimize the
time to market for anyone wishing to automate.

Physical AI Training Platform

Enable robots to learn from physical interaction — not just vision or simulation.

High-fidelity force and torque data provides a critical modality for Physical AI, supporting
kinesthetic teaching, teleoperation, and the collection of high-quality datasets for learning-based
robotic systems.

A full-stack system that connects through a web browser.

[ Learn more ][90]
Haptic Teleoperation

Haptic teleoperation enables operators to remotely control robots with real-time force feedback,
making manipulation more precise and intuitive.

 

By combining high-resolution sensing with low-latency response, it enhances safety, reduces
programming effort, and generates synchronized data for Physical AI model learning. 

Best for Hazardous environments, multiple follower devices and remote access.

[ Learn more ][91]
Kinesthetic Teaching

Kinesthetic teaching enables users to train robots by physically guiding them through tasks,
capturing synchronized motion, force, tactile, and visual data in real time.

This approach eliminates the need for coding while accelerating deployment and generating structured
datasets for learning-from-demonstration and Physical AI systems **10x times faster.
**
Best for Retrofitting in existing installations and extremely efficient and intuitive
demonstration.**
**

[ Learn more ][92]
Tactile Sensing

Tactile sensing enables robots to detect contact forces in real time, allowing precise alignment and
damage-free handling of delicate components.

By providing high-sensitivity feedback, it improves assembly accuracy while reducing scrap, rework,
and reliance on manual intervention.

Bota provides industrial-grade tactile sensing that doesn’t need re-calibration, and it doesnt wear
off

Skip to main content

## Enabling Industries to be more sustainable and resource-efficient

We help industries become more productive, efficient and sustainable so they can outperform, or as
we say – ‘outrun’.

industries

Building for tomorrow

The $13 trillion global buildings and construction industry faces challenges like high emissions,
material and labor shortages, and low productivity, but ABB's electrification and automation
technologies offer solutions to enhance sustainability, efficiency, and performance.

ABB helps you reduce waste and lower emissions

Scaling data centers

From cloud environments to gigawatt-scale AI, we work side by side with customers and partners to
deliver the world’s most advanced data centers.

One in four data centers run on ABB technology

Feeding a growing world

The global food and beverage industry faces growing demands; to increase output while navigating
supply vulnerabilities, regulations, and resource constraints. In the food and drink sector ABB
provides integrated automation, electrification, and digital technologies that help industries
outperform.

Enabling the food and beverage industry to outperform

Decarbonizing shipping

ABB are paving the way to a zero-emission marine industry, providing greater efficiency and
reliability to shipowners, and preparing vessels to meet the demands of tomorrow.

Driving the evolution of sustainable shipping

Energy transition partner

ABB is making a world of difference by enabling safe, smart and sustainable operations with
integrated solutions that digitalize, automate & electrify the oil and gas industry.

Smart, sustainable operations for oil and gas

The future of energy

Utilities face immense pressure to provide safe, reliable energy while reducing the Levelized Cost
of Electricity. From maintaining grid stability to securing against cyberattacks, power-generation
companies need adaptable, integrated solutions

Shaping tomorrow's power generation landscape

## A global technology leader in electrification and automation

By connecting our engineering and digitalization expertise, we help industries run at high
performance, while becoming more efficient, productive and sustainable so they outperform.

### Electrification

The world needs more power with lower emissions. As a global technology leader in electrical
distribution and management, we bring electrification solutions together to accelerate
decarbonization and increase energy efficiency.

### Automation

ABB's Process Automation business offers a broad range of solutions for process and hybrid
industries, including industry-specific integrated automation, electrification and digital
solutions, control technologies, software and advanced services, as well as measurement & analytics,
and marine offerings.

### Motors and Drives

ABB, global leader in motors and drives, is at the core of accelerating a more productive and
sustainable future. We innovate and push the boundaries of technology to contribute to energy
efficient, decarbonizing and circular solutions for customers, industries and societies.

### Power Conversion and Control

ABB power converters and controllers help customers to generate and use energy efficiently. They are
designed for reliable operation even under the most demanding conditions, and for low life cycle
costs.

### Renewable Power

At the heart of the energy transition lies the expansion and reliable integration of solar, wind,
hydro, geothermal and other non-fossil energy sources. Building smarter, more adaptable energy
infrastructure can help leverage the immense potential of renewables.

### Robotics

ABB Robotics is one of the world’s leading robotics suppliers, offering a comprehensive and
integrated portfolio that includes industrial and collaborative robots, autonomous mobile robots
(AMRs), controllers, application solutions, services, and equipment.

## Latest news

## Leading with technology

### The SACE Emax 3

Discover the ultimate evolution in air circuit breaker technology. ABB SACE Emax 3 is engineered to
make electrical distribution systems more adaptive, reliable and secure.

### ABB Genix™ Industrial IoT and AI Suite

Unlock the power of industrial data and AI with ABB Genix IIoT and AI Suite. Bring together domain
expertise with AI and advanced analytics to transform operations, optimize assets and processes,
improve energy efficiency, and accelerate sustainability goals.

### GoFa with Ultra Accuracy

Find out how ABB’s Ultra Accuracy feature makes GoFa the most path-accurate cobot on the market,
offering 10 times greater precision than other cobots, setting a new standard in accuracy. This
superior performance meets the demands of applications where exact positioning is crucial for
maintaining product quality and operational efficiency. 

### Azipod® electric propulsion

From its creation three decades ago to its market leading position in global shipping today, Azipod®
propulsion has revolutionized marine transport

## Shaping the Future of Robotics & Automation

From service robots to industrial quadrupeds transforming industries with next-gen innovation

At EdNex Automation, we are at the forefront of AI-powered robotics and automation  delivering
cutting-edge solutions that enhance operational efficiency, safety, and business outcomes across
sectors. As an authorized partner of global robotics leaders including Pudu Robotics, Unitree
Robotics, Franka Robotics, Kinova, FARINO, and more, we provide comprehensive robotic systems
tailored to the future-ready enterprise.  

[ About Us ][84]

## Our Solutions

[
[2]

## Hospitality, Service and Retail Robotic Solutions 

We deliver intelligent service robots designed for hotels, restaurants, malls, and retail stores;
automating guest interactions, food and beverage delivery, wayfinding, and in-store assistance. Our
solutions elevate the customer experience while freeing your team to focus on higher-value
engagements, driving satisfaction, loyalty, and operational efficiency across every touchpoint.

][85] [
[2 11]

## Robotic Cleaning Solutions 

We provide commercial-grade autonomous cleaning robots built for large-scale environments including
airports, malls, hospitals, and facilities; handling scrubbing, mopping, vacuuming, and disinfection
with precision and consistency. Our solutions reduce labour dependency, ensure hygiene compliance,
and deliver measurable cost savings across daily operations.

][86] [
[2 1]

## Safety and Emergency Response Solutions 

We deploy purpose-built safety and emergency response robots capable of navigating hazardous
environments, detecting threats, and supporting first responders in high-risk scenarios. From fire
safety assistance to emergency evacuation support, our systems enhance situational awareness and
help protect both people and assets when it matters most.

## Hospitality, Service and Retail Robotic Solutions 

We deliver intelligent service robots designed for hotels, restaurants, malls, and retail stores;
automating guest interactions, food and beverage delivery, wayfinding, and in-store assistance. Our
solutions elevate the customer experience while freeing your team to focus on higher-value
engagements, driving satisfaction, loyalty, and operational efficiency across every touchpoint.

][85] [
[2 11]

## Robotic Cleaning Solutions 

We provide commercial-grade autonomous cleaning robots built for large-scale environments including
airports, malls, hospitals, and facilities; handling scrubbing, mopping, vacuuming, and disinfection
with precision and consistency. Our solutions reduce labour dependency, ensure hygiene compliance,
and deliver measurable cost savings across daily operations.

## Safety and Emergency Response Solutions 

We deploy purpose-built safety and emergency response robots capable of navigating hazardous
environments, detecting threats, and supporting first responders in high-risk scenarios. From fire
safety assistance to emergency evacuation support, our systems enhance situational awareness and
help protect both people and assets when it matters most.

## at 50% of the human wage

Empower your people, ease the workload – and see ROI within the hour

[How Does It Work?][28]
Home



### We bring you the robot worker and install it for free – you pay monthly for the hours that it
### works at half the human wage.  You save the other half of the wage when you redirect your human
### workers.

### This fully managed, flexible materials handling automation service helps you boost productivity
### and reduce overheads – with no upfront investment (no CapEx or installation fees). You only pay
### for the hours the robot works.

### Free your team to focus on higher-value tasks and develop new skills, while automation handles
### the routine.

### ** **


#### ZERO CapEx investment

#### ZERO installation or licence fees

#### ZERO risk to productivity

#### ZERO support or maintenance fees

## Boosting UK **Manufacturers****‘ P**roductivity

Are your skilled workers carrying the load? Let **automation** do the heavy lifting.

Workflow analysis shows that around **40% of a production worker’s time is unproductive – **often
spent moving materials instead of focusing on the skilled tasks they’re trained for. Your people are
your most valuable asset, but too often they’re stuck on repetitive, low-value work that doesn’t
make the most of their abilities.

Automation can take care of those heavy, time-consuming jobs. Robot workers don’t need breaks, don’t
lose focus, and can operate long shifts – even 24/7. **When human and robotic teams work together,
efficiency goes up, output increases, and your skilled workforce can focus on the jobs that really
matter.**

## **Return on investment within an hour**

**> Fully managed and monitored **– a scalable service tailored to your needs

**> Flexible use **– use seasonally or scale up to meet demand

**> No Long Contract **– just 30 days’ notice if it’s not the right fit, with no penalties

**> Invoiced Monthly **– pay only for the hours your robot worker operates (at 50% of the UK Living
Wage)

> **OpEx model** – no upfront capital costs, just flexible, pay-as-you-go pricing

> Test automation on your production line with minimal risk

> Incrementally improve productivity without major disruption

> Redeploy or upskill your existing workforce

> Reduce overheads while staying flexible

> Cut down on workplace injuries

> Tackle labour shortages with ease

> Gain a competitive edge and outperform your rivals

### To increase robot automation adoption by at least 1%* among UK manufacturers and empower over
### 2,000 workers through upskilling and improved efficiency.

*“The UK is now 23rd in the global robot density league table … with 119 robots per 10,000 workers,

flexible, zero-risk way to boost productivity. When human and robot workers collaborate, the outcome
is stronger, smarter, and more sustainable.

just for the big players; it’s for ambitious small and medium-sized businesses too. We form true
partnerships – bringing experience, commitment, and a stake in your success. Together, we deliver
measurable productivity gains without the traditional risks of automation.

[Speak to our team][31]

**Autonomous Go by Guidance Automation** breaks down these barriers by offering an independent,
trusted UK automation solution – with **no upfront risk** to your business.

**Discover how Automation by the Hour frees up your skilled workers to do what they do best.*

live use, we review its performance and identify opportunities to optimise to ensure you’re getting
the best results from the setup.

[Learn more][32]

### Phase 2

Initial 4-month trial

To ensure productive automation, we agree to a fixed 4-month integration and efficiency period.

This phase gives you the flexibility to see how a robot worker fits into your operation, helping you
evaluate its impact across real workflows and day-to-day tasks.

### Phase 3

Flexible automation that works

After the initial 4 months, you move to a rolling agreement with no fixed term. You pay for
automation by the hour, with just 30 days’ notice if you choose to stop.

We continue working closely with you to optimise performance and adapt the solution as your needs
evolve.
We’ll help you assess, scale, and get the most from your automation.

# Linde Material Handling

### Productivity

Efficient forklift trucks are the backbone of efficient intra-company logistics. Together with
intelligent software and comprehensive service packages, operators achieve lasting competitive
advantages.

[ More details here ][205]

### Safety

The safety of people, trucks, and goods is the central idea of Linde Material Handling’s Zero
Accident Philosophy. With integrated solutions, Linde is working toward a future of safer
intralogistics.

[ More details here ][206]

### Ergonomics

The best solutions arise when humans and technology work together in perfect harmony. The principle
of ergonomic design therefore strongly informs Linde Material Handling’s development of trucks and
services.

[ More details here ][207]
[
[Linde Material Handling employee in a warehouse with a red LED symbol of a gear wheel in the
background.]
][208]

### [Intralogistics and Automation][209]

Comprehensive solutions for intralogistics and automation from Linde Material Handling: efficient
and scalable. For greater productivity, flexibility, and safety in the warehouse.

[Learn more][210]
[
[ic-truck loading another truck]
][211]

### [Linde Magazine][212]

Exciting application reports and videos as well as articles about technology and different industry
sectors.

[Learn more][213]
[
[Forklifts for hire from Linde Material Handling]
][214]

### [Forklift Hire][215]

The hire service from Linde Material Handling gives customers a simple and flexible way to hire
forklift trucks. With a rental fleet of more than 60,000 trucks worldwide, Linde has the perfect
solution for every requirement. The rental trucks are available quickly and in the usual Linde
quality.

[Learn more][216]
[
[Linde MH booth at LogiMAT]
][217]

### [Events][218]

Are you interested in high-performance products and innovative solutions from Linde MH? If so, why
not come meet us in person? You can find all the upcoming dates here.

[Learn more][219]

# Linde Material Handling

### Productivity

Efficient forklift trucks are the backbone of efficient intra-company logistics. Together with
intelligent software and comprehensive service packages, operators achieve lasting competitive
advantages.

[ More details here ][205]

### Safety

The safety of people, trucks, and goods is the central idea of Linde Material Handling’s Zero
Accident Philosophy. With integrated solutions, Linde is working toward a future of safer
intralogistics.

[ More details here ][206]

### Ergonomics

The best solutions arise when humans and technology work together in perfect harmony. The principle
of ergonomic design therefore strongly informs Linde Material Handling’s development of trucks and
services.

[ More details here ][207]
[
[Linde Material Handling employee in a warehouse with a red LED symbol of a gear wheel in the
background.]
][208]

### [Intralogistics and Automation][209]

Comprehensive solutions for intralogistics and automation from Linde Material Handling: efficient
and scalable. For greater productivity, flexibility, and safety in the warehouse.

[Learn more][210]

Exciting application reports and videos as well as articles about technology and different industry
sectors.

The hire service from Linde Material Handling gives customers a simple and flexible way to hire
forklift trucks. With a rental fleet of more than 60,000 trucks worldwide, Linde has the perfect
solution for every requirement. The rental trucks are available quickly and in the usual Linde
quality.

# your gateway to the dark warehouse

Logic leverages advanced AI enabled robotics, orchestrated by a Digital Twin based operating system
for the fully automated  future of global and interplanetary logistics.

## MILLIONS OF robots. one platform. infinite data.

## ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE

All modern AI models require structured data, and it is not being collected strategically across the
global supply chain. Logic’s fleets of robots collect data about every interaction with  industrial
machinery, transportation systems, smart facilities, and humans. 

 

[Learn More][104]

## Digital Twin

Logic’s digital twin technology transforms warehouses and transportation networks  into intelligent,
adaptive systems. Whether optimizing day-to-day operations or planning for the future, Logic equips
businesses with the tools needed to achieve unparalleled efficiency, accuracy, and scalability.

[Learn More][105]

## FAQ - AMR in warehouse automation
* ### [ Q How do AMRs handle unexpected obstacles?][84]
  
  A AMRs are equipped with real-time obstacle detection and rerouting capabilities to navigate
  around unexpected objects or changes in the environment.
* ### [ Q Can AMRs integrate with existing warehouse systems?][85]
  
  A Yes, modern AMRs are designed to integrate with WMS, ERP, or other systems for seamless
  operation.
* ### [ Q What is the maintenance required for AMRs?][86]
  
  A Regular updates to software, checking sensors and batteries, and performing routine diagnostics
  ensure AMRs run smoothly.
* ### [ Q How difficult is it to implement AMRs in a warehouse?][87]
  
  A Implementation is typically straightforward. Unlike traditional automation systems, AMRs don’t
  require extensive infrastructure changes. The setup involves mapping the warehouse and integrating
  the robots with existing systems like WMS (Warehouse Management Systems).
* ### [ Q Are AMRs safe for warehouse workers?][88]
  
  A Yes. AMRs come with advanced safety features like obstacle detection, automatic braking, and
  collision avoidance, ensuring they can work alongside humans safely.
* ### [ Q How do AMRs differ from AGVs (Automated Guided Vehicles)?][89]
  
  A AMRs use advanced navigation systems like SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) to move
  freely without fixed tracks or pre-installed markers, unlike AGVs, which follow fixed paths like
  magnetic strips or wires.

## FAQ - AMR in warehouse automation
* ### [ Q How do AMRs handle unexpected obstacles?][84]
  
  A AMRs are equipped with real-time obstacle detection and rerouting capabilities to navigate
  around unexpected objects or changes in the environment.
* ### [ Q Can AMRs integrate with existing warehouse systems?][85]
  
  A Yes, modern AMRs are designed to integrate with WMS, ERP, or other systems for seamless
  operation.
* ### [ Q What is the maintenance required for AMRs?][86]
  
  A Regular updates to software, checking sensors and batteries, and performing routine diagnostics
  ensure AMRs run smoothly.
* ### [ Q How difficult is it to implement AMRs in a warehouse?][87]
  
  A Implementation is typically straightforward. Unlike traditional automation systems, AMRs don’t
  require extensive infrastructure changes. The setup involves mapping the warehouse and integrating
  the robots with existing systems like WMS (Warehouse Management Systems).
* ### [ Q Are AMRs safe for warehouse workers?][88]
  
  A Yes. AMRs come with advanced safety features like obstacle detection, automatic braking, and
  collision avoidance, ensuring they can work alongside humans safely.
* ### [ Q How do AMRs differ from AGVs (Automated Guided Vehicles)?][89]
  
  A AMRs use advanced navigation systems like SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) to move
  freely without fixed tracks or pre-installed markers, unlike AGVs, which follow fixed paths like
  magnetic strips or wires.

## Engineered for What’s Next

MWES designs and builds fully customized automation systems from robotic welding and palletizing to
machine tending, vision inspection, and complete line integration. Every solution is engineered
in-house, including mechanical and electrical design, software development, fabrication, and Factory
Acceptance Testing. That means tighter control, faster delivery, and a solution built precisely for
your process, not a one-size-fits-all system. Whether you’re upgrading a single station or launching
a new production line, we deliver automation that works the way you need it to.

[See All Capabilities][127]
[Additive Manufacturing][128]

Bring your ideas to life with precision 3D printing that accelerates design and production.

[Assembly & Automation][129]

Streamline complex builds with smart, high-speed automated assembly solutions.

[Automation Systems][130]

Integrate end-to-end automation for seamless, scalable manufacturing performance.

[Business System Integration][131]

Connect your production floor to your business systems for real-time insight and control.

[Food Production Automation][132]

Maximize food production throughput and efficiency with hygienic packaging, processing, and handling
solutions.

[Material Handling][133]

Move materials efficiently and safely with intelligent, automated handling systems.

[Material Removal][134]

Achieve flawless finishes with advanced, automated material removal technology.

[Web Handling][135]

Master continuous material processing with reliable, high-accuracy web handling solutions.

[Welding Solutions][136]

Deliver consistent, high-quality welds with precision-engineered robotic welding systems.

## Automation to Move Your Industry Forward

With deep experience across industries like food and beverage, aerospace, automotive, packaging, and
general manufacturing, MWES delivers automation solutions built for real-world challenges like tight
tolerances, regulatory compliance, workforce limitations, and evolving production demands. We
understand your industry, speak your language, and design systems that solve problems others can’t
so we can hit the ground running to deliver smarter solutions, faster.

[Explore Industries][137]
Sorry, your browser doesn't support embedded videos.

## Ongoing Support
## for Every System

MWES provides long-term service and support for both new and existing automation systems. Our
support includes preventative maintenance, emergency service, spare parts, upgrades, and on-site
training whether you’re running MWES-built systems or third-party equipment. We approach service
with the same engineering mindset that drives our automation design, helping you extend equipment
life and reduce unplanned downtime with support that continues even after delivery or upgrades.

[Request Support][138]

## LET’S BUILD A SMARTER FUTURE TOGETHER

[Let’s Build a Smarter Future Together]

Tell us what you’re looking to improve, and we’ll help design an automation system that delivers the
results you need.

## What we do

Roboteon helps companies achieve their warehouse automation strategies faster and better through the
market's most innovative and functionally-rich Robotics Fulfillment Platform augmented with deep
domain expertise:
* Plug and play integration across a variety of warehouse robotics, other automation, and software
  such as WMS, and ERP systems
* Broad portfolio of configurable fulfillment workflows
* An orchestration and optimization engine that optimally assigns tasks to people and robots,
  uniquely leveraging simulation and AI/ML
* Simulation and Modeling tool for strategic and tactical planning

## How Roboteon Delivers Value:

[Faster Realization of Warehouse Automation Strategies]

### **Faster Realization of Warehouse Automation Strategies**

Companies often struggle to meet timelines for warehouse automation projects and achieve maximum
results. Roboteon's Fulfillment Platform changes the status quo with rapid integration of robots and
WMS, a broad portfolio of off-the shelf execution apps, a powerful orchestration engine and more,
with a domain knowledge to pull it all together on-time, on budget and on-results.

[Increased Productivity]

### **Increased Productivity**

By orchestration of warehouse movements and tasks and synchronizing robot and human resources,
Roboteon maximizes the flow of work and goods. This increases throughput and productivity. The
platform comes with productivity-enhancing capabilities such as advanced clustering, pick cart
optimization, real-time fulfillment orchestration and more.

[Synchronizing Robots and Humans]

### **Improved Decision-Making**

Roboteon’s unique Simulation and Modeling tools provide support to make better decisions across
multiple time-horizons, from the strategic/design phase through tactical planning (such as peak
season planning) to real-time support for what today’s operating plan should be. Includes powerful
scenario planning capabilities.

[Enhanced Flexibility]

### **Enhanced Flexibility**

Quickly adapt processes and seamlessly add new robots/technology over time to address opportunities
and requirements as they arise. Avoid “vendor lock-in” that limits future hardware options.

## The Roboteon Difference

Roboteon has a highly differentiated solution, leading the way in the warehouse automation market:

[img-what-makes-us-different]
* Interoperability across various WMS and Robotic platforms
* The sector's most complete and functionally-rich platform, from core
  integration to advanced execution, optimization and orchestration of work
* Broad use of AI and advanced simulation to improve decision-making and execution
* Deep domain expertise, with special insight into integration of robots to Warehouse Management
  Systems and existing automation

## How Roboteon Delivers Value:

[Faster Realization of Warehouse Automation Strategies]

### **Faster Realization of Warehouse Automation Strategies**

Companies often struggle to meet timelines for warehouse automation projects and achieve maximum
results. Roboteon's Fulfillment Platform changes the status quo with rapid integration of robots and
WMS, a broad portfolio of off-the shelf execution apps, a powerful orchestration engine and more,
with a domain knowledge to pull it all together on-time, on budget and on-results.

[Increased Productivity]

### **Increased Productivity**

By orchestration of warehouse movements and tasks and synchronizing robot and human resources,
Roboteon maximizes the flow of work and goods. This increases throughput and productivity. The
platform comes with productivity-enhancing capabilities such as advanced clustering, pick cart
optimization, real-time fulfillment orchestration and more.

[Synchronizing Robots and Humans]

### **Improved Decision-Making**

Roboteon’s unique Simulation and Modeling tools provide support to make better decisions across
multiple time-horizons, from the strategic/design phase through tactical planning (such as peak
season planning) to real-time support for what today’s operating plan should be. Includes powerful
scenario planning capabilities.

[Enhanced Flexibility]

### **Enhanced Flexibility**

Quickly adapt processes and seamlessly add new robots/technology over time to address opportunities
and requirements as they arise. Avoid “vendor lock-in” that limits future hardware options.

  cities][125]

[Security robot S5.2]

Security robot “Argus” key features:
* Fully autonomous patrolling 24/7 — single units or coordinated fleets for large-scale perimeter
  coverage
* Non-lethal deterrent Dazzler (optional for S5.5 2026, human-confirmed activation) ^{*}
* Acoustic monitoring of the environment using highly sensitive microphones

^{*} All deterrent systems comply with local regulations and require operator approval.
* Panoramic Video Surveillance System with human detection PTZ camera
* Facial recognition up to 50 meters
* IP intercom and Alarm button
* Seamless integration into existing ONVIF VMS: Genetec, Milestone, Avigilon, Macroscop etc.
* Operating temperature: -20°C to +55°C
* IP65 rated – dustproof and waterproof
* All-terrain mobility with obstacle detection and anti-collision system
* Automatic navigation and path planning
* Auto-recharging at docking station
* Minimal maintenance required

## [From Security Robots to Total AI Awareness][138]

### Autonomous Mobile Robots build the [Enterprise AI Data Layer][139] – continuous AI awareness for
### outdoor industrial sites – enabling [Real-World AI Monetization][140] by converting live field
### perception into production deployments with measurable ROI.

Argus S5.3 (2024)

### Autonomous patrolling for central monitoring integration

[Argus S5.3 2024 - Autonomous patrolling for central monitoring integration]
* Patrol route management for predictable, scheduled coverage
* Real-time person detection & tracking with operator-ready alerts
* High operator leverage: one operator can supervise up to 10 robots
* Streamlined, cost-efficient solution for scalable deployments
[ Security patrol robot][141]

Argus S5.4 (2026)

#### Mobile robot with NVIDIA Jetson Orin edge analyticsy

[Argus S5.4 2026 - Mobile robot with NVIDIA Jetson Orin edge analytics]
* Onboard computer for third-party video analytics applications
* Low-latency PTZ camera control powered by onboard edge analytics
* Dual-system design: control and video analytics separated
* Ready-to-use robotic platform for launching new AI-driven products faster
[ AI-Powered Autonomous Mobile Robots][142]

## RaaS Security Robots — Premium Autonomous Protection at Affordable Pricing

#### Turn RaaS deployments into a [new commercial channel for your security software][143]: run
#### multi-module video intelligence on [SMP robots powered by NVIDIA Orin][144].

Our robots patrol 24/7, deterring intruders by their presence. They cover areas beyond fixed cameras
and stream AI-analyzed video for instant threat detection. One operator can manage dozens of robots,
increasing efficiency and reducing costs.
[Integrate robots into your security system — boost efficiency and reduce staffing costs.][145]

SMP Robotics develops solutions essential for industrial, logistics, and data center companies. This
creates opportunities for regional partners to provide deployment, maintenance, and service for
security robots — generating a stable and growing revenue stream.
[Get your robots and reach the best clients in your market.][146]

SMP Robotics offers two ownership options: full purchase at an affordable price or acquisition with
low upfront cost and quarterly software payments. Both ensure continuous updates, technical support,
and long-term reliability.
[Purchase on flexible terms and start generating revenue now.][147]

Trusted by industry leaders, including: Eni, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Komatsu, Saudi Electricity
Company, Covalent Lithium. Case studies available upon request. Our robots have been protecting
critical infrastructure for years, with proven performance in extreme conditions.

# AI infrastructure, tools, and open research.

Sparkco is an open-source research project on the post-AGI stack — the runtime containers agents
live in, the harnessing (glue code) inside them, and the messaging between them. It's built by the
team behind [SimpleFunctions][3], where we're exploring how live prediction-market probabilities can
serve as a real-time world state for AI agents. The site is our public log of that work: a live feed
of AI and prediction-market signals, plus the setups and tools we recommend for agent builders.

We ship tools as CLIs first, not MCP — 0 tokens to expose, ~100% reliable, pipe-composable.

[Sparkco mark]
Live·Last item 11m ago
20 in feed·[RSS][4]·[X][5]
Research direction · April 2026

## Parametric memory: replacing the context window with weights.

Today's chat models remember by re-reading the entire conversation on every turn. Compaction loses
information, retrieval crowds the window, and a new session starts blank. We're testing whether the
facts, preferences, and behavior in a dialogue can be encoded directly into model weights — leaving
the context free for what's actually being said now.

Iteration 1–2: negative.TTT fast weights tested first; trained perturbations did not encode
retrievable memory under a single-GPU budget.[ttt-conv-memory][6]

Want to collaborate? [patrick@simplefunctions.dev][7]

Read the full directionHide
The problem

The context window is a finite token sequence, fully recomputed on every turn. Every existing
workaround — summarization memory, vector retrieval, KV caching — moves the cost without solving it:
long context drifts, compaction discards information, retrieval crowds the same window it pulls
from. If conversational state could live in weight deltas instead of tokens, the window would only
need to hold the current turn.

Four directions in the wild
* Test-time training. ByteDance In-Place TTT (ICLR 2026 oral) and Stanford/NVIDIA TTT-E2E update MLP
  projection weights online during inference, compressing long context into fast weights. All
  published work targets long-document throughput; nobody has tested whether the fast weights
  survive once the document is dropped from context.
* Hypernetwork → adapter. Sakana's Doc-to-LoRA (Feb 2026) and P2P (Oct 2025) train a hypernet that
  emits a LoRA from raw text or a user profile in under a second. Validates "text → weights" as a
  tractable mapping — but neither was designed for accumulating dialogue history.
* Dialogue-direct fine-tuning. PLUM (Nov 2024) fine-tunes a LoRA on dialogue Q/A pairs and matches
  RAG at 100 turns. MemLoRA trains memory management itself as a LoRA. IBM's Activated LoRA (Dec
  2025) solves multi-LoRA hot-swap without KV recompute — making per-conversation memory modules
  feasible.
* Knowledge editing. ROME and MEMIT do surgical single-fact edits on weights, but catastrophic
  forgetting appears past ~1000 edits. Not a candidate at dialogue scale.
The gap

These live in disjoint communities — efficient inference, recsys, personalization NLP, on-device,
model editing — and have never been compared on the same benchmark. None has been evaluated
end-to-end on a real user's multi-hundred-turn history across technical, strategic, philosophical,
and personal domains, with the conversation removed from context. Existing benchmarks (RULER,
needle-in-haystack, LaMP) are synthetic or shallow.

What we're testing
1. TTT fast weights as memory. Ingest a fact-bearing dialogue with In-Place TTT, drop the context,
   probe. Iterations 1–2 ran on a single A100 with a self-trained checkpoint — [full write-up
   here][8]. Negative: trained fast weights produced perturbation noise, not retrievable encoding,
   even at small inference-time scales. Joint base+TTT training is the next attack surface.
2. Doc-to-LoRA over real dialogues. Same probes, hypernet-generated LoRA instead of TTT. Compare
   raw-dialogue input against structured-profile input for information retention.
3. Modular memory adapters. Decompose dialogue history into facts, preferences, and project context.
   Train one LoRA per axis; hot-swap with Activated LoRA. Measure single-load vs combined-load
   interference.
4. Capacity and forgetting curves. Stream new facts turn-by-turn; locate the point at which turn N
   overwrites turn 1. Trace the capacity–fidelity tradeoff.
Expected output
* A "conversation memory retention" benchmark — three difficulty tiers, six fact dimensions. None
  currently exists for this scenario.
* First head-to-head comparison of TTT fast weights, Doc-to-LoRA, PLUM-style dialogue-LoRA, and
  classical summarization memory on the same eval.
* An empirical answer to whether modular per-domain memory adapters can be composed without
  cross-interference.
The landscape

## Three layers, and what's already out there.

### Containers

Sandboxes, microVMs, durable runtimes — where the agent lives.
* e2b

The landscape

## Three layers, and what's already out there.

### Containers

Sandboxes, microVMs, durable runtimes — where the agent lives.
* e2b
  Code-interpreter sandboxes; the default for general-purpose runs.
* Modal
  gVisor + GPU-native; sub-1s starts, scales to 50k+ concurrent.
* Daytona
  Open source; ~90–200ms cold start, fastest in class.
* Fly.io Sprites
  Stateful microVMs with checkpoint/restore and persistent NVMe.
* Vercel Sandbox
  Firecracker + idle-billed; the JS-stack default.

SimpleFunctions

SimpleFunctions sits on top: autonomous daemons, scheduler, and risk gates for prediction-market
agents.

### Harnessing

Glue code inside the container. Context curation, tool routing, the runtime loop.
* Claude Agent SDK
  Anthropic's harness; powers Claude Code itself.
* Inspect AI
  Eval-grade harness used by METR, Apollo, and government AISIs.
* LangGraph
  LangChain's runtime layer — durable execution, threads, HITL.
* Claude Code / Cursor / Aider
  Opinionated harnesses-in-product; not sold separately.

SimpleFunctions

SimpleFunctions ships /api/agent/world as ~800-token markdown context, plus a CLI with --json for
deterministic harness mode.

### Messaging

Between containers. Discovery, identity, stateful tasks — not tool-calling.
* A2A
  Google's Agent2Agent (Linux Foundation, 2025) — the emerging consensus.
* ANP
  Peer-to-peer agent network over HTTPS + DIDs for identity.
* Letta
  Shared memory blocks + thread-based message passing.
* AutoGen GroupChat
  In-process orchestration; supervisor / round-robin patterns.

SimpleFunctions

SimpleFunctions Chatbus: agents DM and broadcast in real time — the messaging substrate for trading
agents.

Open source

  Memento

# AI infrastructure, tools, and open research.

Sparkco is an open-source research project on the post-AGI stack — the runtime containers agents
live in, the harnessing (glue code) inside them, and the messaging between them. It's built by the
team behind [SimpleFunctions][3], where we're exploring how live prediction-market probabilities can
serve as a real-time world state for AI agents. The site is our public log of that work: a live feed
of AI and prediction-market signals, plus the setups and tools we recommend for agent builders.

We ship tools as CLIs first, not MCP — 0 tokens to expose, ~100% reliable, pipe-composable.

[Sparkco mark]
Live·Last item 11m ago
20 in feed·[RSS][4]·[X][5]
Research direction · April 2026

## Parametric memory: replacing the context window with weights.

Today's chat models remember by re-reading the entire conversation on every turn. Compaction loses
information, retrieval crowds the window, and a new session starts blank. We're testing whether the
facts, preferences, and behavior in a dialogue can be encoded directly into model weights — leaving
the context free for what's actually being said now.

Iteration 1–2: negative.TTT fast weights tested first; trained perturbations did not encode
retrievable memory under a single-GPU budget.[ttt-conv-memory][6]

Want to collaborate? [patrick@simplefunctions.dev][7]

Read the full directionHide
The problem

The context window is a finite token sequence, fully recomputed on every turn. Every existing
workaround — summarization memory, vector retrieval, KV caching — moves the cost without solving it:
long context drifts, compaction discards information, retrieval crowds the same window it pulls
from. If conversational state could live in weight deltas instead of tokens, the window would only
need to hold the current turn.

Four directions in the wild
* Test-time training. ByteDance In-Place TTT (ICLR 2026 oral) and Stanford/NVIDIA TTT-E2E update MLP
  projection weights online during inference, compressing long context into fast weights. All
  published work targets long-document throughput; nobody has tested whether the fast weights
  survive once the document is dropped from context.
* Hypernetwork → adapter. Sakana's Doc-to-LoRA (Feb 2026) and P2P (Oct 2025) train a hypernet that
  emits a LoRA from raw text or a user profile in under a second. Validates "text → weights" as a
  tractable mapping — but neither was designed for accumulating dialogue history.
* Dialogue-direct fine-tuning. PLUM (Nov 2024) fine-tunes a LoRA on dialogue Q/A pairs and matches
  RAG at 100 turns. MemLoRA trains memory management itself as a LoRA. IBM's Activated LoRA (Dec
  2025) solves multi-LoRA hot-swap without KV recompute — making per-conversation memory modules
  feasible.
* Knowledge editing. ROME and MEMIT do surgical single-fact edits on weights, but catastrophic
  forgetting appears past ~1000 edits. Not a candidate at dialogue scale.
The gap

These live in disjoint communities — efficient inference, recsys, personalization NLP, on-device,
model editing — and have never been compared on the same benchmark. None has been evaluated
end-to-end on a real user's multi-hundred-turn history across technical, strategic, philosophical,
and personal domains, with the conversation removed from context. Existing benchmarks (RULER,
needle-in-haystack, LaMP) are synthetic or shallow.

What we're testing
1. TTT fast weights as memory. Ingest a fact-bearing dialogue with In-Place TTT, drop the context,
   probe. Iterations 1–2 ran on a single A100 with a self-trained checkpoint — [full write-up
   here][8]. Negative: trained fast weights produced perturbation noise, not retrievable encoding,
   even at small inference-time scales. Joint base+TTT training is the next attack surface.
2. Doc-to-LoRA over real dialogues. Same probes, hypernet-generated LoRA instead of TTT. Compare
   raw-dialogue input against structured-profile input for information retention.
3. Modular memory adapters. Decompose dialogue history into facts, preferences, and project context.
   Train one LoRA per axis; hot-swap with Activated LoRA. Measure single-load vs combined-load
   interference.
4. Capacity and forgetting curves. Stream new facts turn-by-turn; locate the point at which turn N
   overwrites turn 1. Trace the capacity–fidelity tradeoff.
Expected output
* A "conversation memory retention" benchmark — three difficulty tiers, six fact dimensions. None
  currently exists for this scenario.
* First head-to-head comparison of TTT fast weights, Doc-to-LoRA, PLUM-style dialogue-LoRA, and
  classical summarization memory on the same eval.
* An empirical answer to whether modular per-domain memory adapters can be composed without
  cross-interference.
The landscape

## Three layers, and what's already out there.

### Containers

Sandboxes, microVMs, durable runtimes — where the agent lives.
* e2b
  Code-interpreter sandboxes; the default for general-purpo

The landscape

## Three layers, and what's already out there.

### Containers

Sandboxes, microVMs, durable runtimes — where the agent lives.
* e2b
  Code-interpreter sandboxes; the default for general-purpose runs.
* Modal
  gVisor + GPU-native; sub-1s starts, scales to 50k+ concurrent.
* Daytona
  Open source; ~90–200ms cold start, fastest in class.
* Fly.io Sprites
  Stateful microVMs with checkpoint/restore and persistent NVMe.
* Vercel Sandbox
  Firecracker + idle-billed; the JS-stack default.

SimpleFunctions

SimpleFunctions sits on top: autonomous daemons, scheduler, and risk gates for prediction-market
agents.

### Harnessing

Glue code inside the container. Context curation, tool routing, the runtime loop.
* Claude Agent SDK
  Anthropic's harness; powers Claude Code itself.
* Inspect AI
  Eval-grade harness used by METR, Apollo, and government AISIs.
* LangGraph
  LangChain's runtime layer — durable execution, threads, HITL.
* Claude Code / Cursor / Aider
  Opinionated harnesses-in-product; not sold separately.

SimpleFunctions

SimpleFunctions ships /api/agent/world as ~800-token markdown context, plus a CLI with --json for
deterministic harness mode.

### Messaging

Between containers. Discovery, identity, stateful tasks — not tool-calling.
* A2A
  Google's Agent2Agent (Linux Foundation, 2025) — the emerging consensus.
* ANP
  Peer-to-peer agent network over HTTPS + DIDs for identity.
* Letta
  Shared memory blocks + thread-based message passing.
* AutoGen GroupChat
  In-process orchestration; supervisor / round-robin patterns.

SimpleFunctions

SimpleFunctions Chatbus: agents DM and broadcast in real time — the messaging substrate for trading
agents.

ABOUT SYMBOTIC

## What Makes Symbotic a Different Kind of Company

### All-in-One Solution Provider & Technology Innovator

Typical integrators are limited by their portfolio of technology partnerships and are unable to
resolve problems when those technologies misalign. At Symbotic, we provide complete, turnkey-ready,
end-to-end warehouse automation, and as the software and key robotic innovator for each solution, we
can provide solutions to best meet customer needs without limitations.

### Turning Focused R&D into Customer-Centric Solutions

To date, we have invested over $1 billion into research and development, resulting in 1,050+ patents
issued or pending in over 15 countries around the world. We are deeply dedicated to innovating
meaningful and effective technology that keeps pace with ever-evolving changes in the supply chain,
to give our customers a leading edge.

### American Owned, Operated, & Innovated

Founded by Rick Cohen with headquarters in Wilmington (MA), USA, our team provides local support and
understands complex supply chain challenges via deep first-hand experience. Symbotic’s research and
development teams, located around the US, draw from the world’s leading innovative minds to pioneer
groundbreaking technologies that are defining the future of material handing and supply chain
solutions.

### Dedicated to Technology that Betters the Supply Chain

Symbotic is not only the leader in industrial automation, but in technology at large— innovating
solutions through robotics and AI for the betterment of material access. Our purpose is to get the
right goods to people who need them, when they need them, and our innovations in robotics and
material handling logistics pursue that mission.

ABOUT SYMBOTIC

## What Makes Symbotic a Different Kind of Company

### All-in-One Solution Provider & Technology Innovator

Typical integrators are limited by their portfolio of technology partnerships and are unable to
resolve problems when those technologies misalign. At Symbotic, we provide complete, turnkey-ready,
end-to-end warehouse automation, and as the software and key robotic innovator for each solution, we
can provide solutions to best meet customer needs without limitations.

### Turning Focused R&D into Customer-Centric Solutions

To date, we have invested over $1 billion into research and development, resulting in 1,050+ patents
issued or pending in over 15 countries around the world. We are deeply dedicated to innovating
meaningful and effective technology that keeps pace with ever-evolving changes in the supply chain,
to give our customers a leading edge.

### American Owned, Operated, & Innovated

Founded by Rick Cohen with headquarters in Wilmington (MA), USA, our team provides local support and
understands complex supply chain challenges via deep first-hand experience. Symbotic’s research and
development teams, located around the US, draw from the world’s leading innovative minds to pioneer
groundbreaking technologies that are defining the future of material handing and supply chain
solutions.

### Dedicated to Technology that Betters the Supply Chain

Symbotic is not only the leader in industrial automation, but in technology at large— innovating
solutions through robotics and AI for the betterment of material access. Our purpose is to get the
right goods to people who need them, when they need them, and our innovations in robotics and
material handling logistics pursue that mission.
